blockers.title: The install-root target is named but still lacks one closed signed representation, canonical path input, and checkable later-volume relation
evidence: targetPath.designation says the install-root path is an immutable preselection input 'bound in the signed profile/carrier', but no runtime field, field path, type, serialization, scope (one per closure versus one per profile), or equality rule is defined for that input. The complete profile grammar names only osFamily, architecture, supportedVersionOrBuildSelector, and filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution; tcbCarrier.bindingPoint names only TCB members keyed by that complete profile. 'profile/carrier' therefore asserts a binding without selecting or provisioning its one binding point.

targetPath.derivation delegates to 'ordinary host path resolution'. It does not say whether targetPath is absolute or closure-relative, what anchors it, whether Linux mountinfo selection consumes the lexical signed spelling or a symlink/case/Unicode-resolved spelling, or what stable path/root identity prevents a retarget between observation and use. File 04 lines 145-159 assigns explicit link, case, Unicode, identity, and TOCTOU rules to exact-byte delivery/DR-G07, but this contract neither names a specific verified-root output from that dependency nor fails qualification while that output is absent.

linux.recordSelection says longest prefix of targetPath but does not define decoded mount-point comparison or a pathname-component boundary. For example, a mount point /opt/app is a character prefix of /opt/application while not containing it; raw mountinfo spellings can also differ from the resolved host path. The root record still matches, so the stated missing/ambiguous failure rule need not catch a wrong selection.

filesystemMeasurementTarget.rule requires every relevant resolution to stay on the same designated target and resolutionPredicate step 3 requires an object's volume to 'satisfy' the selected filesystem target. The selected profile retains only a filesystem-type enum or OTHER-FSTYPE digest. No predicate decides whether a second ext4 volume satisfies the target by type or violates it by volume identity, and no target-volume identity is retained for the stronger interpretation.

linux.observerProcess additionally says the verifier's process identity is recorded on the profile, but defines neither the profile field nor the process-identity equality that binds a /proc/<verifierPid>/mountinfo read against PID reuse or process replacement.
blockers.impact: Two implementations can both follow the prose yet bind different lexical/resolved install roots, select different mountinfo records and complete profiles, or disagree over a later object on a different volume of the same filesystem type. The target that gates qualification is therefore not reproducible or independently checkable, and the stronger same-target refusal can silently collapse to a same-type test.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define exactly one signed preselection binding point for the install-root target, including its scope, closed value type/serialization, anchor, and equality. Consume a specifically named stable verified-root/path identity from exact-byte delivery or DR-G07 rather than 'ordinary' resolution, and fail while that dependency is absent. For Linux, bind the stable process/mount-namespace identity, define mountinfo path decoding and component-ancestor comparison over the canonical resolved path, and detect retargeting. Finally decide whether later resolutions must share the exact target volume or only its filesystem-type token; encode and retain the chosen comparison so resolutionPredicate step 3 is executable.

shouldFix.title: companionObservation has a location but can still omit both the observation and the values needed to audit present or mismatch
evidence: The new retainedEventSchema field is 'optional; required iff ... an observation was made'. No rule requires that observation when the active libc evidence carries the signed optional sonameAbi companion, so a producer can make no companion observation, omit the field, and still satisfy the stated iff condition despite the unconditional 'Retained as companionObservation' repair claim.

companionObservationShape makes both soname and abiSelector optional for every presence value. Thus {companionId: SONAME-ABI, presence: present} and {companionId: SONAME-ABI, presence: mismatch} are admitted without the observed pair, leaving neither the alleged presence nor the mismatch independently checkable against the signed companion.
shouldFix.impact: The allow/refuse result remains deterministic because the companion is metadata-only, but the retained compatibility evidence can be absent or content-free while claiming conformance.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State whether observation is mandatory whenever a signed sonameAbi companion is present; if it is, require companionObservation on the corresponding libc event. Give the payload conditional closed forms: absent carries no observed pair, while present or mismatch carries the exact observed soname and abiSelector needed for comparison. If observation is intentionally best-effort, say that and remove the unconditional retention claim.
